Finding.Title: ### F90 — `--run-commands` emits `T-000`, which the plan cannot declare, and a clean cursor then cannot be derived. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
The check ran and was right. The writer is wrong.
`lint --run-commands` records each `MustPassCommand` through `appendCommandRunEvent` (`src/lint/core.ts:501`) and never passes a task. The writer falls back:
``` const task = options.task ?? loose[loose.length - 1]?.task ?? "T-000"; ```
(`src/grace-cursor.ts:2977`.) After a fold, `run/` is empty, so the next command-run is `T-000`. `cursor.unknown-task` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1365–1369`) then fires when `run.xml` names a task the plan does not declare. The same module's position type says *"Known task id only — never a guessed id (A13.2)"* (`src/grace-cursor.ts:252–256`). `T-000` is a guessed id.
Reproduced on run 4 at HEAD of that branch: lint 1 error, `run.xml names task T-000, which is absent from plan.xml`. `ngrace cursor regenerate` dry-run prints `Task: T-000` from the folded ledger. The `--explain` repair ("regenerate from the ledger and plan") re-derives the illegal name. There is no sanctioned edit of a folded ledger.
**The transcript overclaimed "unreachable".** Re-opening a declared task before the post-fold `--run-commands` avoids the fallback. The *written* close protocol does not say that: `ngrace-execute` step 7 runs `--assertions final --run-commands` as the outermost lifecycle gate; step 9 then applies and archives; archive requires `no-open-epoch`. Followed in that order, the sanctioned path emits `T-000`, demands a fold, and leaves `cursor.unknown-task` if the fold is done by opening the sentinel.
**P3.1 as specified does not cover this.** `lifecycle finish` folds loose epochs and writes `applied`. Folding T-000 events without renaming the cursor leaves the same error. The derivation pass for P3.1 has to absorb this, or a small `C-*` has to land first. See the decision candidate below.
**The rule.** A fallback identity the grammar forbids is not a fallback — it is a self-inflicted integrity error. When the close protocol writes a task the plan cannot declare, the checker that then refuses is doing its job; the repair is the writer.
#### Decision candidate — T-000 (not ratified)
Honest options, none free:
- **(a) Do not emit `T-000`.** Inherit a task the plan already declares, or refuse before write. No new lint surface — `src/grace-lint.ts` still has no `--task` flag. Sources, in this order, only when the id is in `planTaskIds`: explicit `options.task` (library callers; not a new CLI flag), last loose event, `run.xml` Task, last folded ledger event. Refuse `invalid-arguments` when none of those is a declared id. Cheap, fail-closed, matches A13.2. Cost: every post-fold `--run-commands` needs a declared task already in scope. The execute skill must say so. - **(b) Declare `T-000` as a permitted system task** the grammar exempts from `cursor.unknown-task`. Makes the fallback legal. Cost: a phantom task in every command-run-only epoch; `status` `tasks=` becomes a lie unless counted separately; A13.2 is weakened for one magic id. - **(c) Auto-terminate command-run events** so they never become the cursor's current task and never require a T-000 open/terminal to fold. Cost: fold semantics grow a special case; "terminal is a judgment" (cursor kinds) is no longer true for this kind.
**(a) is the only option that does not invent a task the plan did not declare.** **Shipped as (a) without the `--task` flag this candidate first proposed**, by [`C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER`](../../../../.ngrace/changes/archive/C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER/) in PR #59 (`49c3c94`).
**Discharged by [`C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER`](../../../../.ngrace/changes/archive/C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER/) (PR #59, `49c3c94`).** `resolveDeclaredCommandRunTask` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:3126–3150`) inherits a `planTaskIds` member from explicit `options.task`, last loose event, `run.xml` Task, or last folded ledger event, and throws `invalid-arguments` when none is declared — *"Cannot record command-run: no declared task is in scope."* `appendCommandRunEvent` calls it at `:2989`. The T-001 fallbacks on `recover --fix` and `maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation` are deleted; both now `inheritLooseEventTask` (`:736–746`) and refuse rather than invent. `cursor.unknown-task` is untouched. No `--task` flag was added to lint (`src/grace-lint.ts` has none); a new lint argv token `task` was a NonGoal (`C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER/spec.xml:587–591`). The bundle's own close is the proof: post-fold `--assertions final --run-commands` wrote events 13–18 as `task="T-003"` (`run-ledger.xml` Epoch-2), not `T-000`.
**Residuals this discharge does not pay**, all stated NonGoals of that spec (`:592–612`) and still true at `49c3c94`: `regenerateCursor` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:802–815`) still re-derives whatever `derivePosition` last-event / last-ledger task is (`:1374–1380`), with no `planTaskIds` check; default `--open-epoch` `from = options.from ?? 1` (`:910`) still holes after a fold ([F90.1](#f90.1) point 3); operator-supplied advance / attempt task ids are still unchecked at write time ([F98](#f98)); the published `@neograce/cli@6.2.0` still invents the sentinel ([F99](#f99)). [F93](#f93) is unchanged.

Finding.Title: ### F90.1 correction — `T-000` is a well-formed task id; the check fires on undeclared, not reserved; the way back exists and is undocumented. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
[F90](#f90) said `--run-commands` emits `T-000`, *"which the plan cannot declare"*, and that *"there is no sanctioned edit of a folded ledger"* / the written close protocol leaves *"no sanctioned way back"*. **Four of those clauses do not survive HEAD.** The writer is still wrong and the checker is still right. What F90 named as the repair, and what it named as unreachable, are not.
**1. `T-000` matches the task grammar.** `ANCHOR_PATTERNS.task` is `/^T-[0-9]{3}$/` (`src/artifact/types.ts:212`). `T-000` is a well-formed task id. A plan *may* declare it. Generators emit `T-001`; conventional plans do not declare `T-000`. That is a convention, not a reservation. F90's phrase that the plan cannot declare the id is false as grammar. It is true of the conventional plan the close protocol produces.
**2. `cursor.unknown-task` fires on an undeclared id, not a reserved one.** `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1361–1370` is `if (!tasks.has(entry.task))` against `planTaskIds`. There is no blacklist. A plan that declared `T-000` would silence the code for that id. A repair that exempts `T-000` from the checker — F90 candidate (b) — would therefore be the wrong repair even if it were ratified: it would punch a hole in a check that is doing its job, for an id the grammar already accepts. Candidate (b) is more clearly wrong than F90 stated, not less.
**3. The way back exists and is undocumented.** After a poisoned `T-000` command-run, `cursor advance --task T-001 --kind terminal` *without* `--open-epoch`, then `cursor fold`, leaves `run.xml` on a declared task. Fold's auto-open (`src/grace-cursor.ts:1081–1087`, `maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation` at `:730`) inherits the last loose event's task; a trailing declared terminal makes that task `T-001`. The same sequence is already in the suite: `src/grace-cursor.test.ts:2966–2967` advances `kind: "terminal"` with no `openEpoch` after a post-work `appendCommandRunEvent`, then folds. F90's *"no sanctioned way back"* is an overclaim. **No *documented* way back is true, and still damning** — `ngrace-execute` steps 7 and 9 (`skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md:40–43`) still run `--run-commands` after fold and then archive, and nothing in that contract names the terminal-without-open-epoch recovery. An operator following the written order still walks into the trap F90 measured.
The natural reread of "re-open a declared task" does **not** work. Default `--open-epoch` sets `from = options.from ?? 1` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:896`). After a prior fold, `nextEventId` takes `ledgerMax + 1` (`:3047–3051`). The new opened event lands at that id with allocation `1..id+98`. `validateEventsAgainstAllocations` (`:2536–2540`) then refuses `range hole at 1`. The suite already knows: `:2976` comments *"default from=1 would hole"* and computes `from = maxFolded + 1` by hand. That is why the recovery has to be *no* default open-epoch.
**4. The `T-001` fallbacks F90 never named.** F90 cited `appendCommandRunEvent`'s `?? "T-000"` at `src/grace-cursor.ts:2977`. Two siblings invent `T-001` by the same A13.2 shape:
| Writer | Line | Fallback | |---|---|---| | `recover --fix` | `src/grace-cursor.ts:616` | last loose task, else `"T-001"` | | `maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation` | `src/grace-cursor.ts:730` | last loose task, else `"T-001"` |
After a `T-000` command-run they *inherit* `T-000` (not a new guess). The `T-001` fallback is the same defect on the empty-`run/` path. A repair that changes only `:2977` and leaves these two is this repository's repeated one-site patch.
**What this does and does not do to [F90](#f90).**
- **Stands.** The writer invents a task id. The checker is right to refuse an undeclared one. The written close protocol emits `T-000` after fold, and archive then permits (`[F93](#f93)`). Candidate (a) — do not emit a guessed id; refuse when none is in scope — is still the only option that does not invent a task the plan did not declare. Not re-ratified here; still not ratified there. - **Overturned.** "The plan cannot declare `T-000`." A blacklist of `T-000` as the repair. "No sanctioned way back." - **Narrowed.** "No sanctioned way back" → no *documented* way back. The verbs exist; the contract does not name them.
Those three clauses are this correction's effect on [F90](#f90) at the time it was written. The writer-invents clause and "still not ratified" are now paid; see the writer-half paragraph below. The archive-permits half is still [F93](#f93).
**Scheduled as `C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL`, already authored on `fix/cursor-task-sentinel` at `241c628`** (`.ngrace/changes/active/C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL/spec.xml` on that branch; not present here). That spec absorbs these four points (its Problem states them) and forbids exempting a sentinel id. This pass does not create or edit that bundle.
**The writer half is paid.** `C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL` was superseded (F83 close-criterion trap) by `C-CURSOR-TASK-IDENTITY`, which was superseded (F64 write-scope miss) by `C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER`, which shipped [F90](#f90) candidate (a) in PR #59. Point 3's range hole and the regenerate re-derivation of an undeclared last event remain, as that spec's NonGoals (`C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER/spec.xml:600–612`).
**The rule.** A well-formed id the plan did not declare is an undeclared id, not a reserved one. Do not repair a guessed fallback by making the guess legal.

Finding.Title: ### F27.1 amendment — F27's headline is stale; `C-DECLARED-WRITES` paid it. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
[F27](#f27)'s title still reads *"`ObservedWriteScope` is declared and digested, but never compared."* That was true when written and is false now. `C-DECLARED-WRITES` shipped **both** halves the finding asked for, and `src/review/core.ts:155` names F27 as its subject. Two codes exist today:
- `review.scope-outside-write-scope` — repository changed files against the plan's declaration (`src/review/core.ts:1033`). - `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` — durable `WriteEvidence` paths, the tool-generated git digests on cursor attempts, against the same declaration (`:1097`).
Measured on `C-SUPERSEDE-VERB` after execution: `ngrace review --change C-SUPERSEDE-VERB` returns **three** findings, two of them naming `scripts/release-check.ts`, one from each audit. The scope audit reports *"ran over 48 changed file(s) against ObservedWriteScope … 2 out-of-scope"*. Nothing about this is silent.
**F27's body is still accurate and its headline is not.** The body enumerates the `scope.*` shape and overlap checks and `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope`, and says *those* never compare the declaration to what was written. That remains true. The headline generalizes to every surface, and `review` is now a counterexample.
**Why this is worth its own entry.** A reader who cites the headline without reading the body will restate a paid defect as a live one. That is exactly what the authority did in [F120](#f120), twice in one session, and it produced a recommendation that the product already forbids. A finding whose defect was later paid should say so in its first sentence; this ledger has no convention for that, and the absence is now a measured cost, not a tidiness complaint.
**Observed while measuring, not yet ruled.** The changed-file audit flags `docs/plans/**` edits — the authority's own roadmap commits — as out of scope for whatever bundle is active, while the `WriteEvidence` audit filters that prefix (`src/review/core.ts:1066`). So finding one on this bundle is `decisions.md`, which no bundle will ever declare. Whether the changed-file audit should adopt the same filter is a question for the bundle that takes this area, not something to fix in passing.

Finding.Title: ### F180 — the retirement engine is inert in both directions: nothing annotates eligibility, and the shipped derivation would find nothing if it ran. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `67bc55c`, corrected the same day after the executor disproved the authority's first version.
**Three separate gaps, each measured.**
1. **Nothing annotates.** **0 of 214** live findings carry a `<PaidBy>` child; all **25** retired ones do. Nothing writes that element when a paying bundle archives. 2. **Validation never derives.** The validation path reads the stored child (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:673`); `collectPaidBy` (`:372-410`) runs **only** in the `--split` path (`:489`). 3. **The derivation is too narrow to fire even if it ran.** Constructing `RegistryRow`s from `registry.xml` ∪ `registry-retired.xml` and calling the **shipped** `collectPaidBy`: 36 rows in, map size **24**, and **0** live-eligible. The rule reads `row.pays` **only**, and only for rows whose `statusText` matches `/delivered|superseded/i`. 4. **No operation exists.** `--split` is the only mode and refuses once `decisions.md` is a stub (`:477-478`, exit 1).
**So the ratchet is the only working half.** `D28.1` calls eligibility *the enforcement* and the ceiling merely *the backstop*; in the shipped engine the backstop is load-bearing and the enforcement cannot fire at all.
**The authority's first version of this finding was false, and the error is instructive.** It claimed *"twelve live findings are eligible under the engine's own rule"* — `F100`, `F105`, `F108`, `F108.1`, `F108.2`, `F109.1`, `F112`, `F113`, `F125`, `F155.1`, `F157`, `F9.1`, occupying **477** lines. Those entries are live and their registry rows do discuss paying them, but **none is in the shipped map**. The authority reimplemented `collectPaidBy` instead of importing it, and applied the F-token regex to each row's **entire text** — `Charter` and `StatusText` included — where the shipped rule reads **`Pays` alone**. Same tokens, wrong field: the fourth *right-string-wrong-position* error of that session. Disproved by the executor's `WRONG`, then re-verified by importing the real function.
**What that changes.** Widening the derivation is not a refinement, it is the difference between an enforcement that can fire and one that cannot. Whether to widen it — for instance to rows whose `Pays` names an archive directory, or to a `Closed with` clause in `StatusText` — is a **spec decision** for [`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`](#named-bundle-registry), and it must be argued against `D28.1` rather than assumed. **Never cite the twelve as an eligible set.**

Finding.Title: ### F181 — the rulings headroom is smaller than one session's decisions, and the decisions genre has no reachable retirement trigger. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `67bc55c`.
`rulings.xml` is **1668** lines with `headroom="75"` (2 × the 37.5-line median H2 decision) and `ceiling="1743"`. The three decisions staged from this session alone — [D27.1](#d27.1), [D32](#d32), [D33](#d33) — are **115** lines of prose, **121** with element wrappers. Flushing them gives **1789**, a breach of **46**.
**Partial flushes fit and are arbitrary:** `D32` alone lands at 1697; `D32` plus `D33` at 1735, eight lines under. Choosing which ratified decision to withhold from the record is not a decision the ratchet should be making.
**Wrapper arithmetic corrected 2026-09-06**, after this entry first read 127 / 1795 / 52 and 1699 / 1739. An element occupies `bodyRaw` lines **plus three** — the open tag, the `Title` line, and the close tag — because `<Body>` and `</Body>` land on the blank lines that `parseFrozenMarkdown` keeps at the head and tail of every body (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:225-243`, which trims nothing). Per entry that is 54 / 29 / 38, not 56 / 31 / 40. The original figures added two per entry. The headline of this finding is unaffected: 121 still exceeds the 75-line headroom by more than half again, and the breach is real.
**The genre has no reachable trigger.** Decisions retire on `CodifiedIn` or `TaughtIn` ([D28.1](#d28.1), [D31](#d31)). **Zero** live decisions carry either — by design, since `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` made historical tagging a NonGoal owned by a later bundle. So the decisions genre can **only grow** until that bundle lands, while its headroom is sized at two median entries.
[D27.1](#d27.1) is the sharpest case: its own text says it is *"born codified"* and a `CodifiedIn` candidate the moment the tag ships. The tag has shipped. It could be tagged and retired on arrival — but tagging is another bundle's scope, so the entry that documents its own retirement cannot be retired.
The headroom was derived at split time as a multiple of the median entry, which measures **entry size** and not **arrival rate**. This session produced 8 findings and 3 decisions; the findings headroom of 252 lines was also exceeded by the 267 lines of findings alone, and is only survivable because findings have a working trigger. Sizing headroom from arrival rate rather than entry size is the open design question.

Finding.Title: ### F183 — the clamp makes retirement unable to create room, so the record still cannot be flushed after `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** on the delivered working tree, by exercising the validator against a copy of the post-`--retire` record.
`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` did what it specified: the one-time exception fired and `rulings.xml` went `1668/75/1743` → `1624/259/1883`. The rulings half of the flush now fits — 1624 + 161 = 1785 against 1883, with 98 lines spare.
**The findings half does not, and never could have.** `findings.xml` went `8279/252/8531` → `7726/252/7978`, because the ceiling is recomputed as `min(previousCeiling, newBase + newHeadroom)` on every move. Retiring 15 findings removed 553 lines of content **and 553 lines of ceiling**. The staged findings are 341 lines wrapped; 7726 + 341 = 8067 against a ceiling of 7978.
**The breach is 89 lines before the bundle and 89 lines after it** — 8279 + 341 = 8620 against 8531, and 8067 against 7978. This is not a regression; it is the half the bundle did not address. The structural fact is that `ceiling = base + headroom` is re-derived at every move, so **retirement never creates room for growth**. The headroom is the only room there will ever be, permanently.
**The named remedy is unavailable.** Probed on a copy: the untouched post-move record validates clean (exit 0), and adding 336 lines of well-formed findings trips `ceiling-exceeded: live findings line count 8062 exceeds persisted ceiling 7978; --retire / move the eligible entry to the retired sibling`. All 15 eligible findings were retired by this bundle, so 0 remain, and raising the ceiling is explicitly not the remedy.
**No partial flush exists.** The genres are entangled in both directions: 10 citations from staged finding entries to staged decisions, and 9 from staged decision entries to staged findings. Flushing either genre alone leaves dangling fragments, which `validate-citation-anchors.ts` exits 1 on.
**Root cause is [F181](#f181)'s, unchanged:** headroom is sized from **entry size**, not **arrival rate**. `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` corrected that for rulings by moving the multiplier 2 → 7. Findings has shipped `7 ×` since the split, and `7 × 36 = 252` is still smaller than one to two sessions of findings arrival — 341 lines from 11 staged entries.
**The authority approved the spec on arithmetic that used the pre-clamp findings ceiling** (`8027 ≤ 8531`), never applying the clamp it had verified in the same pass. The spec's Problem section and the executor's unblock table carry the same error. Owner: a follow-on bundle, which depends on the exception and clamp machinery this bundle ships. The open design question is how to size a headroom against arrival rate without re-creating a budget that can be raised to pass ([D28.1](#d28.1)).

Finding.Title: ### F186 — the one-time ceiling exception can fire again, because a clamped rewrite persists an arbitrary headroom. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `1896592`, by driving the shipped predicate. Raised by the executor against the authority's claim that the exception was spent; the authority had cleared it on a false premise and re-measured only when challenged.
`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` shipped `isFirstRulingsRewrite` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:504-513`): persisted headroom equals `2 ×` the median live H2 `Decision` **and** persisted ceiling strictly below persisted base plus `7 ×` that median. It was accepted on the argument that after the first rewrite the persisted headroom is `7 × median`, so re-firing would need the median to more than triple — 129.5 against a largest live H2 of 61.
**That argument assumed a headroom the code does not always write.** `persistSnapshot` (`:867`) sets
``` headroom = ceiling === formulaCeiling ? computedHeadroom : ceiling - base ```
so **whenever the clamp binds**, headroom is persisted as `ceiling − base` — an arbitrary residue, not `7 ×` anything. The guard then reduces to a coincidence between that residue and twice a median.
**Reachable, not theoretical.** Calling the shipped predicate with the live H2 set: at persisted base **1809** under a ceiling pinned at **1883**, headroom is `1883 − 1809 = 74 = 2 × 37`, the predicate returns **true**, the clamp is disabled and the ceiling rises to **2068** — a raise with no ratified decision, which is the act [D28.1](#d28.1) forbids. Exactly one base in `[1600, 1883]` re-fires at median 37, so the target is narrow; it also moves with the median, giving roughly one live value per cycle. Base 1809 is **+185** lines from the 1624 that shipped, and the staged decisions alone are 157.
**The authority's error, recorded against the finding that carried it.** The clearing argument was given to the maintainer as measured safety. It was a structural inference from one branch of a ternary, never checked against the other. [CLAUDE.md](../../../../CLAUDE.md)'s standard — read an artifact's definition before giving it a role in an argument — applies to code paths as much as to artifacts.
Owner: `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`, which removes the predicate outright rather than leaving it dormant.

Finding.Title: ### F187 — the retirement window ships with no fuel, and the findings that would fuel it are stuck in the buffer. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** on the delivered `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW` working tree, by driving the real binary against a throwaway record.
**The mechanism works.** A `--retire` that moved 18 lines took the findings window from **252 to 270** — `H + Δ_retired`, exactly as designed. Under the shipped formula the ceiling would have dropped to 7960 and the window would have stayed 252, so retirement really did create room for the first time. The anti-ratchet holds: a second `--retire` moved 0 and left the file byte-identical.
**It cannot act.** Production has **zero eligible findings** (`validate-record-retirement.ts` exits 0), so `Δ_retired = 0` and the window stays at `H = 252`.
**The ceiling is pinned, so the window can only be opened by retiring *before* the content arrives.** `ceiling = min(previousCeiling, Base_live + H)` can never exceed the 7978 already persisted: once the file grows, the clamp binds and holds 7978. So the window is `7978 − base`, and flushing first then retiring gains nothing — the clamp caps the ceiling while the base has already risen.
**The arithmetic, at this date.** Staged findings wrap **494** lines (494 under the anchor-boundary convention, 504 under the trailing-trim one; the conclusion is identical). To flush them the base must fall to `7978 − 494 = 7484`, from **7726** — so **242 lines of findings must be retired first**, and zero are eligible.
**The circularity.** The findings that would become eligible are themselves in the buffer. The staged charter row for `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` pays [F180](#f180) and [F181](#f181) (78 lines) and that bundle is archived, so they become eligible **the moment they are flushed** — which is the act that is blocked. This bundle's own row pays [F183](#f183) and [F186](#f186) (81 lines), eligible once it archives.
**No available sequence fits.** Flush everything and immediately retire the 78 eligible lines: base `8220 − 78 = 8142` against a ceiling clamped at 7978 — a breach of **164**. Add this bundle's 81 once it archives: **83** still over. Every intermediate state is CI-red, and `validate:ci` carries the validator.
**What would close it:** roughly **242** lines of live findings becoming eligible, which happens only as future bundles archive and their registry rows name live findings in `Pays`. Eligibility remains the enforcement ([D28.1](#d28.1)) and that is the intent — but it means the flush waits on unrelated bundles, while the buffer grows by every session that records a finding. Four arrived in the session that measured this.
Owner: a maintainer decision, not a code defect. `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW` delivered what it specified.

Finding.Title: ### F195 — a test runs `--retire` against the production record and mutates it whenever anything is newly eligible. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07**, during the close of `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS`, immediately after the archive `git mv`.
`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` calls `runValidator(REPO_ROOT, ["--retire"])` at two sites and then asserts the production record is byte-identical — the "a second `--retire` writes no byte" probe. That assertion holds **only while nothing is eligible**. The moment something is, the test does not observe a no-op: it **performs the retirement**.
**Observed, not theorised.** Archiving a bundle makes its own live registry row's `name` equal an archive directory, which is the registry eligibility trigger. Running the targeted suite straight after the `git mv` therefore exited 1 **and moved the row**: `registry.xml` lost `name="C-CODIFY-DECISIONS"` and went `base="13" headroom="13"` → `base="12" headroom="14"`, while `registry-retired.xml` gained it with `status="retired"`. Re-runs then passed 4/4, because the mutation had already happened. The working tree carried a record change that no operator performed.
**The resulting state was correct, which is what makes it dangerous.** The row *should* retire once its bundle is archived, so nothing looked wrong afterwards and the diff was easy to mistake for intended close work. A test that silently performs a governed record operation is indistinguishable from one that observes it, until the day the operation is not the one you wanted.
**It is destructive by construction at exactly the moment it runs.** Close ceremony archives a bundle and then re-runs the suite as post-archive evidence — so the newly-eligible-row condition is not an edge case, it is the routine state at every close that archives a bundle carrying a live charter row.
Remedy is for a later bundle to decide: run the no-op probe against an isolated fixture rather than `REPO_ROOT`, or assert eligibility is empty before invoking, or drop `--retire` from the assertion and compare a dry run. Related to the same file's earlier defect of pinning a mutable production count, which was removed under `F123`'s "counts expire"; this is the mutating sibling of that mistake.

Finding.Title: ### F194 — the `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` charter row was falsified again, by the bundle it charters. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07** on the delivered `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` working tree, after `T-003` corrected the two phrases it was authorised to correct.
`T-003` fixed the occupancy claim and the census that [F192](#f192) recorded. The bundle's own work then falsified two further sentences in the same row, which `T-003` was not authorised to touch and correctly left alone:
- *"the rulings call site still clamps against the post-move base"* — `T-001` changed exactly that, giving the rulings snapshot the pre-move `ceilingBase`. - *"`TaughtIn` versus `CodifiedIn` is unresolved"* — the approved spec resolved it: `TaughtIn` annotates and does not retire.
**The authority's error, and it is the second instance on this one row.** The standing rule is to **authorise the sweep, not a phrase list** — "change only X" leaves known-false text standing, so the authorisation must cover whatever X falsifies. The plan brief named two phrases; the bundle invalidated two more. [F192](#f192) recorded the same failure one dispatch earlier, when a claim written twice in the row was corrected once.
The maintainer ruled that the remedy rides in a chartered bundle rather than a standalone correction commit, so that record edits keep bundle discipline. Owner: the next bundle, chartered as *correct every sentence in that row which a bundle has falsified* — scoped by what invalidated it, never by an enumerated phrase list.

Finding.Title: ### F192 — the `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` charter row contradicts itself, because a claim written twice was corrected once. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-07** at `cd8500f`, raised by the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's own text and confirmed by reading the live row.
The row in `registry.xml` carries two false statements, both authored by the authority, and they sit in adjacent paragraphs alongside their own refutation:
- *"that genre is already forty lines over its window"* — **false**. Measured `<Rulings base="1834" headroom="49" ceiling="1883">`: the live size is **49 under** its ceiling, not forty over. The same row says *"both genres fit their windows today"* three lines earlier. - *"59 live, zero tagged"* — **65** live. The number was written before the flush that landed `D27.1` and `D32`–`D36`, and went into the record stale.
**How the first one survived.** The claim appeared **twice in one row** — once in the ratification paragraph explaining why the position was deferred, once in the charter paragraph. When [F191](#f191) falsified it, the authority corrected the charter paragraph and left the ratification paragraph standing. This is [F136.1](#f136.1)'s pattern at a smaller scale: *a list that appears twice can be wrong twice, and fixing the copy you happened to look at leaves the other*. The lesson generalises from module lists to any claim restated within a single artifact.
**A related staleness, recorded so the pattern is visible.** The authority also told the maintainer, across two exchanges, that *codifying decisions cannot open the rulings window* — because the rulings call site clamps against the post-move base. That was **true at the pre-flush equilibrium**, where `base + H` equalled the ceiling exactly, and **false immediately after the flush**, which moved the base to 1834 and put the genre into the clamped regime where the window grows by `Δ` until `Δ` reaches about 210. Same defect class as the row: a measurement correct when taken, restated after the state it described had moved.
Remedy is two phrases in one live registry row. Owner: the maintainer's call on whether it rides with `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS`, whose own charter row it is, or goes as its own correction.

Finding.Title: ### F39 — Lint reports 118 artifacts clean; 8 of them are not well-formed XML. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Found the same way as [F38](#f38): an executor doing the ordinary thing, reporting a workaround it did not have to mention. Authoring `C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE`'s plan it wrote `--explain` inside the `DESIGN` comment block, noticed the artifact still linted clean, removed the `--` sequences anyway because they are not well-formed, and said so in one line of its report.
**Measured across the whole artifact tree:**
``` artifacts scanned: 118 (ngrace lint: "XML artifacts checked: 117, Errors: 0") rejected by expat: 8 C-FLAG-HONESTY/plan.xml C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT/plan.xml C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE/plan.xml C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE/plan.xml C-DECLARED-WRITES/plan.xml C-REPORT-HONESTY/plan.xml C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE/plan.xml C-ESCALATION-HONESTY/plan.xml ```
Cause is uniform: `--` inside an XML comment. XML 1.0 §2.5 forbids it; `fast-xml-parser` accepts it and expat rejects it. The three sites checked are `--name`, `recover --fix`, and `--format only:` — CLI flags, in comments, in a repository whose entire subject is a CLI.
**Why this is systemic rather than incidental.** The plan convention in this roadmap is a binding `DESIGN` comment block, and the thing being designed is a command-line tool. Every flag is a `--`. The collision is guaranteed by the two conventions meeting, and it has already happened in **eight of the archive's plans** without one error.
**The defect is the honesty of the report, not data loss.** The product's own parser reads these files correctly; nothing is broken today. What is false is the line `XML artifacts checked: 117 / Errors: 0`, which claims a validity that was never checked. Any other consumer — `xmllint`, an editor, a CI validator, a parser in another language — rejects them. That is [F10](#f10)'s shape at the tool level: a name claiming more than the body verifies.
**Open question the repair must settle, recorded because it shapes the bundle.** Adding a well-formedness check turns eight **archived** artifacts red, and archived bundles are immutable in this repository. So the check cannot simply be switched on: it must be scoped to active bundles, or emitted as a warning with the archive grandfathered, or the archive's immutability re-examined. Whichever is chosen must be argued rather than assumed — a check that quietly excludes the eight files that motivated it would be its own [F28](#f28).

Finding.Title: ### F172 — the citation validator's qualifier-suffix slug is file-local, so splitting a duplicate-token pair across live and retired makes CI red. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06** at `11e2d51`, on the authority's verification of the `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` draft spec, by probe rather than by reading.
`expectedSlugFor` (`scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts:49-71`) applies the `-correction` / `-amendment` / possessive qualifier **only when `duplicateCount > 1`**, and that count is computed over **the file being read** (`parseHeadings`, `:95-102`). The record holds exactly three duplicate heading tokens — `F19`, `F21`, `F27.1` — whose second member carries a qualifier id.
Whole population, each entry moved alone into a genre file and validated:
| id | exit | message | |---|---|---| | `f19` / `f21` / `f27.1` | **0** | ok | | `f19s` | **1** | `anchor id "f19s" does not match slug grammar (expected "f19")` | | `f21-correction` | **1** | `expected "f21"` | | `f27.1-amendment` | **1** | `expected "f27.1"` |
Both members kept in one file: exit **0**. So the refusal discriminates on the split, not on the copy.
**Why this bites the split.** The draft spec requires genre files to repeat the heading with **a copy of the same anchor**, requires same-file rules to apply per genre file, and forbids rewriting the slug grammar. A correction typically outlives the paid original, so eligibility puts one member in `findings.md` and the other in `findings-retired.md` — the exact case that fails. Three of the four available remedies are closed by the spec's own Constraints; the spec must rule between pinning duplicate pairs to the same layer and authorizing a file-local single-occurrence qualifier.

Finding.Title: ### F21 — The fix budget counts attempts; the execution contract says it counts failures. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`countTaskAttemptEvents` (`grace-cursor.ts:1563`) filters `kind === "attempt"` with **no outcome condition** — the code says so deliberately (*"Counter itself has no outcome/signature condition (A19.1)"*). Escalation fires at `grace-cursor.ts:1737`:
```ts if (options.outcome === "fail" && attemptCount >= FIX_ATTEMPT_BUDGET) // FIX_ATTEMPT_BUDGET = 2 ```
So the rule is: *a fail that is the second-or-later **attempt** of any outcome in the window.*
`skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` says **"two failed attempts"** in four places — rule 5 (`:38`), the `attempt` kind (`:65`), and the `escalation` kind (`:90`, `:92`). **Those are different rules**, and the contract's version is the one every executor is handed.
**The divergence is latent, not what happened here.** Measured from this epoch's ledger, T-001's attempts ran `fail`(2) → `pass`(3) → `fail`(5) → escalation(6) → resume(7) → `pass`(8): two real failures, so both rules agree that event 5 escalates. The divergence bites on a **pass-first** sequence — `pass, fail` reaches `attemptCount = 2` and escalates on the *first* failure, which the contract says should not happen. Under red-first discipline that sequence is ordinary: a task whose first cycle needs no red, then a genuine red for a later criterion.
The escalation message compounds it — `grace-cursor.ts:2320` renders *"Budget exhausted for T-001 after 3 attempts"*, reporting a count of attempts under a name ("budget exhausted") the contract defines in failures. The executor read it as a second failure and was right by accident.
**This is F12's class exactly: the contract does not describe the protocol the CLI enforces** — found again in the very skill file `C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT` was written to make complete. That bundle documented the *kinds*; it did not verify the *thresholds* the prose asserts. **A completeness check over the kind set does not check the sentences around it.**
Disposition: follow-on queue. Which side moves — code to match "two failures", or contract to match "second attempt" — is a real design question and is **not** settled here. The authority's leaning is that the code is right and the prose is wrong: an agent that has already burned two verification cycles on one task is worth a checkpoint whatever the outcomes were. But that is a preference, and this is a finding, not a decision.

Finding.Title: ### F21 correction — the attempt budget was renamed and narrowed, not deleted. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**This entry was itself wrong on first writing, and the corrected text is below.** The first version claimed `FIX_ATTEMPT_BUDGET` was simply gone and that `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4` was the only budget and the only escalation site. That was produced by a grep for the old name and the distinct-signature name — **neither of which could match the constant that actually replaced it.**
**What the product does, measured at `6335e3f`.** `src/grace-cursor.ts` declares **two** budgets:
``` FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2 (:177) FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4 (:183) ```
`decideFixBudgetEscalation` (`:1683`) evaluates **trigger R before trigger D**: R fires when the current signature has occurred `>= 2` times in the window under **exact kind plus key equality**; D fires when the window holds `>= 4` distinct signatures.
**So [F21](#f21)'s substance holds and its constant does not.** F21's real finding was that the counter was *outcome-blind and signature-blind* — any second attempt in the window, of any outcome, armed the escalation. That behaviour is genuinely gone: the repeat budget now requires the **same** signature. What survives is a repeat budget of 2, which the first correction erased.
**Consequence for planning, and it cuts the other way from [F56](#f56).** F56 caps *distinct* reds per task at 3. Trigger R adds a second, independent cap: **a task may never plan the same signatureKey twice in one window.** Two reds in a task are safe only because their keys differ — which is exactly why `C-SCHEMA-REFERENCE`'s `T-001` and `T-003` executed without an escalation. A plan that reddened the same criterion twice would pause on the second fail.
**`ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` is accurate on all of this** and always has been. Lines 38, 65 and 90 state both triggers, and line 65 explicitly rules out "any two fails regardless of signature". Canonical and packaged are byte-identical. An executor has now reported this file as stale on the fix budget **twice**, both times wrongly; the likely cause is that the sentence leads with "2 failed attempts" and the qualifying clause reads as droppable.
**The rule, sharpened.** A finding that quotes a constant is a measurement with an expiry date — but re-measuring by grepping *the name the finding used* only proves that name is absent. **A rename is indistinguishable from a deletion under that grep.** Verify the behaviour at its decision site (`decideFixBudgetEscalation` here), not the identifier, before reporting a mechanism gone.
